sources.entry: Countly Community Edition - Real time mobile and web analytics, crash reporting and push notifications platform. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Countly server is a self-hostable, privacy-focused analytics platform that collects session, event, crash and push-notification data from mobile, web and desktop apps.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the server-side part of Countly. It collects sessions, views and events and reports on them through built-in reports and customizable dashboards. It covers crash and error reporting for iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, NodeJS, Unity, Java and Javascript, plus rich push notifications for iOS and Android. Other listed features include remote configuration, in-app rating widgets, email reports and alerts, hooks that forward data via email or webhooks, a Data Manager, and a Compliance Hub for consent and data subject requests. A read and write API is provided, and the dashboard itself is built on the read API. Functionality is extended through a plugin architecture.
use_cases: crash and error reporting for apps
sending push notifications to iOS and Android users
consent management and data subject requests for compliance
building custom analytics dashboards and email reports
how_to_run: wget -qO- | bash (installer script for Ubuntu or CentOS, as given in README; URL omitted in source)
Alternatively, run bin/countly.install.sh from the countly-server package on a fresh Ubuntu/CentOS/RHEL server
Docker: use the official Countly Docker repository and its installation instructions (Countly Lite)
notable: Privacy-first, self-hosted or private cloud deployment with full data ownership
Plugin-based architecture for extending or adding features
Read and write APIs; the dashboard is built on the same read API
Compliance Hub for consent collection and data subject requests
Write API allows sending data from any source, not just official SDKs
caveats: Installer script assumes a fresh Ubuntu, CentOS or RHEL server with ports 80 or 443 free and open
Editions differ: the open-source Lite edition is for free non-commercial use, while Enterprise and Flex are paid tiers with advanced features and SLA
Security issues must be reported by email rather than GitHub issues
keywords: track app users on my own server
